title: Etale and Zariski quasi-coherent higher direct images agree
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Let $M$ be a quasi-coherent module on $(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}})$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Under the equivalence of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], let $M_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ be its quasi-coherent Zariski module, obtained by restriction to open subschemes, and write $N_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the associated small etale module of a quasi-coherent Zariski module $N$. For every integer $q\geq0$ there is a canonical isomorphism of small etale module sheaves, natural in $M$,
$$ R^qf_{\mathrm{et},*}M\;\cong\;(R^qf_{\mathrm{Zar},*}M_{\mathrm{Zar}})_{\mathrm{et}}. $$
The Zariski higher direct image on the right is quasi-coherent. Both higher direct images are computed by injective resolutions in the respective categories of all structure-sheaf modules; Zariski direct image is as in [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], and etale direct image is as in [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors].

source.place: Tag 071N, lemma-higher-direct-images-small-etale, etale case; the associated-module equivalence is proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent, part (2).

proof.text: Put $F=M_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. The equivalence identifies $M$ canonically with $F_{\mathrm{et}}$ and identifies its restriction to an etale $a:W\to X$ with $(a^*F)_{\mathrm{et}}$. Set $N_q=R^qf_{\mathrm{Zar},*}F$. Clause (1) of [lem-pc-finite-support-hi] proves that every $N_q$ is quasi-coherent, using only the stated quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $f$, with no quasi-compactness assumption on $Y$. Thus $(N_q)_{\mathrm{et}}$ is defined.

source.place: Tag 071N, lemma-higher-direct-images-small-etale, first sentence; Tag 03DX, proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent, part (2)

proof.text:
For an etale $g:U\to Y$ put $X_U=X\times_YU$, $p_U:X_U\to U$ and $a_U:X_U\to X$. The chart limit defining direct image is evaluation at $X_U$: a compatible chart family is exactly a section on $X_U$, since $X_U$ itself is its terminal chart. Choose an injective module resolution $M\to I^\bullet$. Consequently $(f_{\mathrm{et},*}I^n)(U)=I^n(X_U)$ with its $\mathcal O_U(U)$-action. Kernels are computed objectwise and images in sheaves are sheafifications of presheaf images. Therefore the cohomology sheaf of this complex is the module sheafification of
$$P_q(U)=H^q(I^\bullet(X_U)).$$
Its restrictions are induced by $I^\bullet(X_U)\to I^\bullet(X_V)$. Compose the derived-evaluation/slice comparison with the module/abelian evaluation comparison on the slice to identify this group with $H^q((X_U)_{\mathrm{et}},M|_{X_U})$: the slice $X_{\mathrm{et}}/X_U$ identifies with $(X_U)_{\mathrm{et}}$, and its restricted ring is $\mathcal O_{X_U}$ since both evaluate on a chart $W$ as $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$. The module sheafification interface gives the linear universal map $P_q\to R^qf_{\mathrm{et},*}M$. This is the quotient-of-cocycles computation, rather than an assertion that evaluation commutes with sheaf cohomology.

source.place: Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images, proof, kernels and images of evaluated injective resolution; descent.tex Tag 071N, slice convention

proof.text:
For every $U$, the equivalence in Step 1 identifies $M|_{X_U}$ with $(a_U^*F)_{\mathrm{et}}$. Apply [lem-sfb-qcoh-cohomology-etale-pullback-naturality] to obtain the canonical linear identification
$$P_q(U)\cong H^q(X_U,a_U^*F).$$
This is an identification of presheaves of modules, not merely of separate groups: for $h:V\to U$ over $Y$, the map $X_V\to X_U$ is etale (it is a morphism between etale $X$-schemes, as in the slice equivalence); the cited comparison commutes with exactly this restriction. Its linearity identifies the $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$-actions via $p_U^\sharp$. It is also natural in $F$.

source.place: Tag 071N, proof, replacement of etale cohomology by Zariski cohomology using Tag 03DW

proof.text:
Suppose $U$ is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), $p_U$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its higher images of $a_U^*F$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-pc-finite-support-hi](1). By [pqf-lem-affine-vanishing] all their positive cohomology on $U$ vanishes. Hence [lem-pc-leray-degenerate-sections](2) makes the canonical edge map an isomorphism
$$H^q(X_U,a_U^*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(U,R^qp_{U,*}a_U^*F).$$
No separatedness of $f$ or $X_U$ is used. Since $g$ is etale, it is flat by definition. The sheaf form of [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] gives $g^*N_q\xrightarrow{\sim}R^qp_{U,*}a_U^*F$. Composing the inverse on sections with the edge map gives $P_q(U)\cong\Gamma(U,g^*N_q)=(N_q)_{\mathrm{et}}(U)$.

source.place: Tag 071N, last paragraph; coherent.tex Tags 01XK (lemma-quasi-coherence-higher-direct-images-application) and 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology)

proof.text:
The affine identifications are compatible with arrows: write $\epsilon_U$ for the edge map and $b_U$ for flat base change. For $h:V\to U$ between affine etale objects, let $\rho$ denote pullback of the cohomology class and $\sigma$ restriction on sections of $g^*N_q$. The section formula of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-map-sections] gives the compatibility of edge classes with each base change (here $h$ is an etale $U$-scheme by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] applied to $Y$, hence flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism], and the second projections are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]). Applying that formula to $g$, $h$ and $gh$, and using composition of pullback on their representing cochains, gives $\epsilon_V\rho\epsilon_U^{-1}b_U=b_V\sigma$: both composites pull back the same representing cocycle and then pass to its sheaf cohomology class. Thus $b_V^{-1}\epsilon_V\rho=\sigma b_U^{-1}\epsilon_U$. Together with Step 3 this is the required presheaf compatibility; all maps also commute with a map $F\to F'$.
Every etale object has an affine open cover by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. On an arbitrary $U$, restrict a class of $P_q(U)$ to its affine opens and apply these identifications. On overlaps the results agree, as may be checked on affine opens of the overlap; the sheaf condition for $(N_q)_{\mathrm{et}}$ glues them uniquely. Hence there is a natural linear map $P_q\to(N_q)_{\mathrm{et}}$ which is bijective on affine objects. It is locally surjective, and any section of its kernel is locally zero, using the same affine covers. Its sheafification is therefore an isomorphism: local lifts glue uniquely after sheafification. By Step 2 this is the claimed canonical $R^qf_{\mathrm{et},*}M\cong(N_q)_{\mathrm{et}}$, natural in $M$.

source.place: Tag 071N, final sentence; canonical maps in coherent.tex Tag 02KH and cohomology.tex Tag 01F4
